newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE-Lomax out because of alleged assault case.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-Lomax out because of alleged assault case.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Sept 17 - Rugby league test prop John Lomax made himself unavailable for the Kiwis' series against Papua New Guinea and Great Britain next month because of a pending court case against him, coach Frank Endacott said on Tuesday.
Lomax and former Canberra player Mark Lowry were allegedly involved in an incident with a doorman at a nightclub in the New South Wales country town of Orange late last month, NZPA reports.
Both league men were charged with assault and their case has been set down to be heard in Orange on October 10 -- in the middle of the series against the Kumuls.
Endacott said Lomax had told him about the court case.
"I knew about it and I was asked by the player to keep it confidential but it looks as if someone got it out of the Canberra camp," Endacott told NZPA.
"I'd spoken to Johnny about the whole thing and I could tell he wouldn't be able to concentrate on his football during the test series.
"It was going to be difficult for him, it is already difficult for him but we made a mutual decision."
He said Lomax, who has had probably his worst ever season on and off the field, needed to address his problems first before concerning himself with test football.
The Kiwi prop was banned twice this year in the Optus Cup for illegal tackles as well as sustaining injuries which kept him out for much of the season.
"It is sad for Johnny, he is still a good player -- that doesn't go away regardless of what has happened to him this year," Endacott said.
"But he does need to have a good look at what is going wrong and change things accordingly.
"We'd love to have had him, but he's got other things on his mind and it is probably best that he deals with that first."
Lomax's place in the Kiwi test team has gone to rookie South Queensland Crushers' prop Grant Young.
Young, who moved to Queensland as a teenager, will play for the Auckland Warriors next season.
